provenance: Issue #20 reconstruction of the wheeled, suspended, iron-capped timber ram described by Vitruvius (via Battering ram). Not a measured surviving machine. Small external dimensions retain the accepted #18 model. Large dimensions are a geometric estimate at equal moving mass per assigned operator (32/6); no historical claim for demon staffing or strike speed.

sources.use: Historical construction: wheeled wooden frame, suspended timber, metal cap and bands; consulted 2026-09-26.
English oak average dried density 675 kg/m3; moisture/species variation is not represented; consulted 2026-09-26.
Iron near-room-temperature density 7874 kg/m3, used as an approximation for historical fittings; consulted 2026-09-26.

approach_note: Provisional slow operator-controlled playtest movement, not measured historical performance. Configurable per machine.
speed_note: Author decision 2026-09-26: demonic velocity derived halfway between the small ram's reinforced and armored zero-damage thresholds; large ram uses the same contact speed. Shared Impact Physics and gate response stay unchanged.
cadence_note: Recovery lasts one gravity-pendulum period from the accepted model's 36 MU suspension span. This is a reconstruction estimate, not historical cadence data. Demonic power supplies strike acceleration.
